title: A Battery’s Second Career
section: 讲话 / 报道 / 讲座
transcript:
A battery removed from an electric vehicle may still store a considerable amount of energy. The question is whether that remaining ability is suitable for a different job. A car needs to respond rapidly to changing demands, while a stationary battery supporting a building may charge and discharge more gradually. However, transferring used batteries between these settings is not simply a matter of changing the label.

An engineering class examined a proposed system for a workshop with rooftop solar panels. The owner wanted to store some electricity generated during the afternoon and use it after sunset. Used vehicle batteries appeared cheaper than new units, but their histories varied. Two batteries of the same age could have experienced very different temperatures and charging patterns.

The students first measured how much energy each battery could hold. They then tested how its temperature changed during charging and how quickly stored energy was lost while it was idle. One unit performed well on capacity but became unusually warm under a moderate load. The group excluded it from the proposed system because capacity alone did not establish safe, predictable behaviour.

The remaining units were arranged so that a weak unit could be disconnected without stopping the whole installation. This increased the initial cost of controls and monitoring. Nevertheless, it reduced the chance that one deteriorating battery would make the entire collection unusable.

The lecturer emphasised that reuse must be evaluated across the whole system. Cheap components can require expensive testing, maintenance and eventual recycling. A second life may still make economic and environmental sense, but only if those additional demands are included. The workshop proposal was therefore treated as a question of system design, not merely a bargain purchase of discarded equipment.

questions.prompt: Why might a used vehicle battery be useful in a building?
options: Buildings need no monitoring of stored energy.
Stationary use may place more gradual demands on it.
A battery regains all its original capacity after removal.
Solar panels prevent every form of battery deterioration.
questions.answer: Stationary use may place more gradual demands on it.
questions.explanation: 固定储能的充放电需求可能比车辆行驶更平缓，因而适合部分退役电池。

questions.prompt: Why were batteries of the same age not assumed to be equivalent?
options: They had different labels attached to their cases.
They had all been produced for different countries.
Their temperature and charging histories could differ.
Their owners had paid different electricity prices.
questions.answer: Their temperature and charging histories could differ.
questions.explanation: 相同年龄的电池可能经历不同温度和充电方式，状态不能仅凭年龄推断。

questions.prompt: Why was one battery excluded despite good storage capacity?
options: It became unusually warm under a moderate load.
It had been stored in the workshop overnight.
It could not be painted to match the other units.
It charged only when the sun was visible.
questions.answer: It became unusually warm under a moderate load.
questions.explanation: 该电池在中等负载下异常发热，容量良好并不代表安全稳定。

questions.prompt: What does the lecturer recommend considering in a reuse decision?
options: Only the purchase price of the discarded batteries.
The appearance of the rooftop panels.
Only the number of batteries collected.
The costs and demands of the complete storage system.
questions.answer: The costs and demands of the complete storage system.
questions.explanation: 讲师要求把测试、监控、维护和回收等整个系统成本一并考虑。
